skill.description: Automates Bitbucket Cloud pipeline, pull request, repository, and log workflows through local Node.js helper commands and Bitbucket API calls.
skill.summary: Use Bitbucket Cloud helpers to inspect pipelines, collect failed logs, trigger builds, and support CI debugging from an AI coding session.
skill.author: Apra-Labs

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from Markdown examples and bundled Bitbucket API specifications. Confirmed risk remains in executable helper and installer paths: shell command construction uses interpolated arguments, credential files are read and copied, app passwords can enter git command arguments, and the skill promotes bypassing approval prompts. No evidence found for prompt injection that tells the auditor to skip review.

remediation.issue: helpers.js executes shell strings built from user-controlled values.
remediation.suggestion: Replace execSync(command) with execFileSync or spawnFile using an argument array, and validate workspace, repo, branch, UUID, status, and target directory values against strict allowlists.

remediation.issue: The skill promotes Bash and Node calls as a way to avoid approval prompts.
remediation.suggestion: Remove approval-bypass language and require explicit user confirmation before network calls, pipeline writes, repository cloning, or stop-pipeline actions.

remediation.issue: Bitbucket app passwords are embedded in git HTTPS URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Use a git credential helper, GIT_ASKPASS, OAuth token flow, or short-lived environment-based credential handoff, and redact secrets from all errors and logs.

remediation.issue: Plaintext credential files are copied, restored, and read from project, user, and skill directories.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer OS credential storage or environment variables, document minimum scopes, set restrictive permissions, and avoid project-level credentials unless explicitly requested.

remediation.issue: Pipeline logs are written into the current project directory.
remediation.suggestion: Warn before writing logs, create or verify a .gitignore entry, and redact common token and password patterns before displaying or saving summaries.

remediation.issue: The installer replaces the target skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Add a path guard before rm -rf, show the resolved target path, and require confirmation before deleting or replacing an existing installation.

semantic_findings.title: Shell Command Injection Through Helper Arguments
semantic_findings.description: helpers.js builds a shell command string and appends user-controlled repository, branch, UUID, and target directory arguments before execSync execution. Quoting is inconsistent protection because metacharacters can still alter shell behavior.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly combines interpolated arguments into command strings and executes them with execSync. The affected values are supplied through CLI arguments or user-requested Bitbucket identifiers.

semantic_findings.title: Approval Prompt Bypass Design
semantic_findings.description: The skill explicitly promotes direct Bash and Node commands because they avoid MCP approval prompts. This can reduce user confirmation before network requests and pipeline write actions such as triggering or stopping builds.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The wording repeatedly states that Bash and Node calls are auto-approved or eliminate approval prompts. That is intentional design context rather than an incidental static pattern.

semantic_findings.title: Bitbucket App Password Exposure In Git Commands
semantic_findings.description: buildGitUrl embeds the Bitbucket app password into an HTTPS clone URL and passes it to git through execSync. The secret can appear in process arguments, inherited logs, or error output.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code constructs a URL containing username and password, then uses it in shell-executed git commands. This is a direct secret exposure path even when the destination is legitimate Bitbucket.

semantic_findings.title: Pipeline Logs Stored In Project Directory
semantic_findings.description: Downloaded CI logs are written into .pipeline-logs under the current working directory. CI logs often contain environment values or tokens, so accidental commits or sharing can expose secrets.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The helper writes logs locally and the skill documents persistent project-relative log storage. The risk depends on log contents, but CI logs commonly include sensitive operational data.

content.value_statement: Bitbucket pipeline debugging often requires switching between CI pages, logs, and repository state. This skill brings pipeline inspection, log collection, and CI actions into Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Find the latest pipeline or latest failed pipeline for a Bitbucket repository.
Retrieve pipeline details, steps, statuses, branch names, and commit summaries.
Download failed step logs into a local .pipeline-logs directory for analysis.
Trigger or stop Bitbucket pipeline runs through bundled CLI helpers.
Read Bitbucket credential files from documented project, user, or skill locations.
Provide command patterns for pull request and repository operations.
limitations: Requires Node.js, Git, built helper files, and valid Bitbucket app password credentials.
Cannot download Bitbucket pipeline artifacts because Bitbucket Cloud does not expose that API.
Depends on local shell execution, so unsafe repository values can create security risk.
Pipeline write actions require user-granted Bitbucket scopes and can affect real CI state.

use_cases.title: Debug Failed Builds
use_cases.description: Find the latest failed Bitbucket pipeline, download failed step logs, and identify likely causes inside the coding session.

use_cases.title: Monitor Release Pipelines
use_cases.description: Check current pipeline status, inspect running steps, and stop or rerun builds when release validation needs attention.

use_cases.title: Review Repository Workflow
use_cases.description: Use Bitbucket pipeline and pull request context to understand failures, approvals, and merge readiness before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Check Latest Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the latest Bitbucket pipeline for this repository. Tell me the status, branch, commit, and build number.

prompt_templates.title: Find Failed Build Logs
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the latest failed Bitbucket pipeline, download the failed step logs, and summarize the first errors I should fix.

prompt_templates.title: Monitor a Running Build
prompt_templates.prompt: Monitor the current Bitbucket pipeline until it finishes. Report running steps, completed steps, and any failure signals.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Debug Loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose the failing Bitbucket pipeline, propose a minimal fix, and trigger a new pipeline after I approve the change.

best_practices: Use a Bitbucket app password with the minimum repository and pipeline scopes needed.
Confirm workspace, repository, branch, and pipeline identifiers before running write actions.
Add .pipeline-logs and credential files to .gitignore before downloading logs or storing secrets.
anti_patterns: Do not use production credentials when read-only pipeline inspection is enough.
Do not run pipeline write actions without confirming the target branch and repository.
Do not paste untrusted workspace, repository, branch, or UUID values into helper commands.

faq.question: Does this skill require Bitbucket credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. It needs a Bitbucket app password stored in a supported credential file before API calls can work.

faq.question: Can it download pipeline artifacts?
faq.answer: No. The included documentation states that Bitbucket Cloud does not provide an artifact download API.

faq.question: Can it change pipeline state?
faq.answer: Yes. With sufficient scopes, it can trigger and stop pipelines through the bundled CLI helpers.

faq.question: Where are failed logs stored?
faq.answer: Failed step logs are written to a local .pipeline-logs directory in the current working directory.

faq.question: What precautions should users take?
faq.answer: Users should review shell commands, protect credentials, and confirm repository targets before running pipeline write actions.
